parts.text: Describe observation as a research method.

parts.text:
Design an alternative investigation which tests smells and facial attractiveness as an
observation and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.text:
Evaluate this alternative way of studying smells and facial attractiveness in methodological
and practical terms.

text: Demattè et al. used a laboratory experiment to investigate smells and facial attractiveness. An
alternative way to investigate smells and facial attractiveness would be to conduct an observation.

parts.text: What is meant by the ‘behaviourist perspective’ in psychology?

Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Bandura et al. conducted a study to investigate the causes of aggression.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘longitudinal method’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Rosenhan (sane in insane places)
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)
Freud (little Hans)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What are the problems when carrying out studies using the longitudinal method?

Haney, Banks and Zimbardo (prison simulation)
Milgram (obedience)
Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the qualitative results collected in each of these studies.

What problems may psychologists have when they collect qualitative data in their studies?
